included: signed application identity, authorization, and connector continuity
excluded: mdbase-rs collection semantics except where invoked at an authority boundary
cloud infrastructure implementation, which is maintained in the private mdbase-cloud-ops repository
an independent security assessment or penetration test

trustBoundaries.title: Application-signed authorization ceiling
trustBoundaries.authority: The application installation signs the maximum requested authority; the portal may narrow it but cannot broaden it.

trustBoundaries.title: Stable application and connector identity continuity
trustBoundaries.authority: A stable application installation key signs each fresh grant request; applications pin the connector public key on first successful authorization and reject silent replacement.

trustBoundaries.title: Application-to-connector encrypted relay
trustBoundaries.authority: The control plane routes authenticated ciphertext; the connector decrypts and then applies its exact local grant.

trustBoundaries.title: Local connector policy enforcement
trustBoundaries.authority: The user-owned connector is the final authorization and filesystem boundary for computer-owned collections.

trustBoundaries.title: Control-plane authentication, consent, and routing
trustBoundaries.authority: The portal selects and narrows grants; server routing checks cannot replace the final connector or hosted-provider check.

trustBoundaries.title: Hosted-provider authorization and content encryption
trustBoundaries.authority: The hosted provider verifies the exact replica capability and proof before decrypting and executing through mdbase-rs.

trustBoundaries.title: Hosted data-key wrapping
trustBoundaries.authority: AWS KMS wraps only per-collection data keys under an exact environment, purpose, collection, and envelope-version context.

trustBoundaries.title: Immutable release and artifact integrity
trustBoundaries.authority: Release workflows build from an immutable tag and publish checksummed, attestable artifacts; unsigned previews are labelled explicitly.

cryptographicConstructions.construction: P-256 ECDSA with SHA-256 and canonical 64-byte IEEE-P1363 low-S signatures over a domain-separated, length-delimited transcript
cryptographicConstructions.binding: protocol, authorization, application, manifest, stable installation signing identity, fresh grant agreement and signing keys, flow, nonce, lifetime, redirect and state, PKCE challenge, requested operations and files, and optional collection

cryptographicConstructions.construction: P-256 ECDH, separate HKDF-SHA-256 request and response keys, AES-256-GCM, and a monotonic counter encoded into the 96-bit nonce
cryptographicConstructions.binding: protocol, suite, grant, application, connector, collection, scope epoch, key ID, request ID, direction, operation, and counter

cryptographicConstructions.construction: Random 256-bit per-collection DEK with AES-256-GCM and a random 96-bit nonce; HMAC-SHA-256 keyed path tokens
cryptographicConstructions.binding: kind-specific associated data binds ciphertext to collection, resource, record, file, sequence, replica, mutation, transfer, or import identity

cryptographicConstructions.construction: P-256 ECDSA with SHA-256 over a newline-delimited request transcript with canonical base64url fields and a five-minute freshness window
cryptographicConstructions.binding: method, target, body digest, credential digest, timestamp, and UUID nonce

cryptographicConstructions.construction: AWS KMS symmetric Encrypt/Decrypt of locally generated 256-bit DEKs in a bounded self-describing envelope containing the immutable key ARN
cryptographicConstructions.binding: service, environment, purpose, collection identity where applicable, and envelope version

permitted: opaque account, application, connector, grant, collection, and routing identifiers
requested operation and exact grant policy
protocol, replay counter, timing, status, and bounded ciphertext sizes
hosted metadata explicitly documented in docs/encryption.md
prohibited: relay operation inputs, results, or connector diagnostics in plaintext
tokens, private keys, unwrapped data keys, credentials, and proof signatures in logs

knownLimitations.description: This package has not been reviewed by an independent security assessor.
The design does not protect plaintext after an authorized application receives it or an unlocked collection from a fully compromised user account.
Relay routing metadata, operation names, timing, network addresses, and ciphertext sizes remain observable.
The standard hosted provider can decrypt collection content; private zero-knowledge hosting is not implemented.
There is no append-only public key-transparency log.
A future native application SDK still needs platform-keystore storage; browser keys are non-extractable and the desktop is a daemon presentation client.
Render currently uses rotated, least-privilege AWS access keys rather than workload identity federation.
The relay broker is a single managed service; tested recovery is automatic reconnect after broker restoration, not uninterrupted high availability.
The isolated full database, object, KMS-replica, retained-key, and clean-environment recovery drill remains open.
Canonical platform signing and notarization are not yet configured.
Recovery administration currently depends on one human operator and has no independent recovery or security contact.

Inspect log, trace, error, crash, and support paths for prohibited data.
Review dependency, build provenance, artifact verification, and secret-handling boundaries.
Report findings with source location, exploit preconditions, impact, and a reproducible test.
